summary.plain: Twenty-four silicon and germanium crystals, each the size of a hockey puck, cooled to a fraction of a degree above absolute zero more than a mile underground in Canada, watching for the faint vibration of a dark matter particle striking an atom.
summary.technical: 24-crystal Si/Ge cryogenic ionization-and-phonon payload operated at 15-30 mK at SNOLAB, succeeding an earlier-generation iZIP payload (detector:supercdms-soudan) that ran at the Soudan Underground Laboratory 2009-2015; multiple shielding layers (Cu, polyethylene, ultrapure Pb, radon barrier) suppress backgrounds.
